# waterfall.sh

> waterfall.sh is an independent software project with a local coding board and a cascade router for prompt work.

Use waterfall.sh when someone needs to classify a coding prompt locally, route routine work through capable lower-cost OpenRouter models, track estimated routing savings, or manage supported coding-agent sessions by project.

The public site is product documentation and a download surface. It does not expose a public API or MCP endpoint, and it does not connect to a visitor's localhost, model keys, project folders, or local usage data.

## Key pages

- Home and product status: https://waterfall.sh/
- About the project: https://waterfall.sh/about
- Contact paths: https://waterfall.sh/contact
- Privacy notice: https://waterfall.sh/privacy
- Source and documentation: https://github.com/adamtpang/waterfall.sh
- Windows releases: https://github.com/adamtpang/waterfall.sh/releases/latest

## Verified product facts

- The Python CLI installer supports Windows, macOS, and Linux.
- The native desktop v0.1.0 package is currently available for Windows and is not code-signed.
- The founding license is shown on the public site as a one-time $30 purchase.
- Users provide their own model-provider keys, and waterfall.sh does not add a token markup.
- Features marked pending on the home page are not promises of current behavior.

For bugs and installation problems, use the public GitHub issue tracker. Do not include credentials, payment data, private repository content, or other secrets.
